content.intro: This lesson covers Excel and Web APIs as part of Excel Developer Tools, Integrations, and Extensibility. It follows the attached Excel curriculum, with an emphasis on small examples and verification.
content.why_it_matters: Excel and Web APIs contributes to reliable business reporting and professional spreadsheet delivery. Document assumptions, verify results independently, and separate optional platform tools from core Excel behavior. Compatibility: Power Query, the Data Model, Power Pivot and DAX are related but distinct capabilities; their exact availability varies by Excel edition, operating system, license and update channel. Follow the course’s local availability checklist before building a dependent workflow.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Excel and Web APIs focuses on the following parts of the supplied syllabus: API concepts and structured responses; JSON data preparation; Power Query web connectors; Authentication, privacy, and connection restrictions. Keep the underlying source data visible and make each assumption explicit.

content_blocks.run_instructions: Use a locally configured Office Add-in development environment and supported host. The excerpt is inspectable source, not executable in a plain worksheet or this browser.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Work in a duplicate workbook or a scratch sheet. Restore the input range and formula/code to the original state, clear filters or selections, then rerun the same test cases. Record expected and actual behavior rather than assuming a successful result.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a small worksheet or workbook section that demonstrates excel and web apis. Use clear headers, label units and assumptions, and capture expected versus actual output for a normal case and an edge case. Where the concept requires a specialized Excel feature, first verify that feature is available in your Excel edition.

task_acceptance_criteria: The worksheet/workflow uses a clear, labeled source range and explicit assumptions.
The learner records an expected output and independently compares it with the actual result.
At least one relevant edge case is checked; data and formula errors are not silently concealed.
The workbook is saved as a copy and compatibility/security/accessibility notes are followed where relevant.
hints: Reduce the problem to a small range with known values before scaling it up.
Inspect cell values and formulas, not only displayed formatting; verify data types, references and range boundaries.
Compare expected versus actual results and check the Microsoft documentation for version-specific functions or tools.
content.expected_output: In a configured Excel Office Add-in, writes a label to A1 and synchronizes changes. Requires the Office.js runtime and a valid add-in project.
common_mistakes: Assuming the displayed format is the same as the stored value or data type.
Using an incorrect range boundary, a mismatched lookup key, or an unverified assumption.
Trusting a result without comparing it with a known calculation or checking a failure/edge case.
